document.title: Read Markdown diffs as rendered Markdown, with the changed words marked
document.summary: A Markdown file in a review renders as Markdown and still shows what changed: old blocks in red, new blocks in green, changed words marked, code blocks as line diffs.
document.why: [PR #197](source:s1) says a skill's Markdown is hard to read in a line diff: a paragraph is one long line, so a two-word edit shows as a whole red and a whole green line. The owner's review then asked for the same view in the full file viewer, for HTML and images to render, for code blocks with line diffs and colors, and for word marks without a percent or time limit.

sources.label: PR #197
sources.title: Read Markdown diffs as rendered Markdown, with the changed words marked

lookFor: Read the skill rewrite in the demo the [PR](source:s1) links, and judge if the word marks on rewritten paragraphs help or are noise.

groups.title: Rows and word marks
groups.summary: `markdownRows` in `markdown-diff.ts` splits both sides of a file into blocks and uses git's hunk lines to pair them into context rows, change rows, and code rows. `wordMarks` marks the words that differ.

attention.note: `joinEdits` replaces the 60% rule and the 150 ms limit. Two changes join when the words kept between them are no longer than either change, and `unitMarks` gives no marks to a block with no word kept. A paragraph that was mostly rewritten now shows marks on most of its text, where before it showed only its tint. Decide if that reads better on your skill diffs.

notes.body: HTML in the Markdown becomes nodes of the same tree (`raw`), then `sanitize` keeps only what GitHub allows.
One old and one new code block with different text: a `code` row, drawn as a line diff.
The size of a run counts the letters of its words. Punctuation has no size, so a kept comma does not split a change.

fileNotes.package.json: `fast-myers-diff` replaces `diff`. `hast-util-raw` and `hast-util-sanitize` read HTML. `shiki` and `decode-named-character-reference` were in the tree and are now imported by the Vite config.
fileNotes.src/ui/lib/markdown-diff.test.ts: Covers the rows, the join rule, a long text with nothing in common, and what the sanitizer drops.

groups.title: Rows are made off the main thread
groups.summary: `markdownRowsJob` in `markdown-rows.ts` sends both sides of a file to `markdown.worker.ts` and resolves with the rows, or with `null` when the worker fails.

attention.note: The rows are made in the browser, in a worker, and not when the CLI writes the payload. Making them in the CLI would add the Markdown and HTML parsers to its runtime dependencies, which today are `zod` only. The worker chunk is 339 kB before gzip. Decide if you want the rows in the payload after all.

notes.body: Every waiting job gets `null`, so each file falls back to its source diff.

fileNotes.vite.config.ts: The browser build of the entity decoder reads `document`, which a worker does not have. The alias picks its plain build.
fileNotes.src/ui/lib/markdown.worker.ts: One message in, one message out. A throw in the parser becomes `null` rows.

groups.title: The rendered rows
groups.summary: `MarkdownDiff` draws the rows in one column or two. A code block goes through Pierre (`PierreSnippet`, `PierreSnippetDiff`), an image loads from the web or from git, and a link that does not open says why.

attention.note: `imageTarget` loads a web image as it is, so a hosted review calls the image's host. A path in the repository loads only when the image is part of the change: the payload has no other images, and those show their alt text with the reason. Decide if the payload must hold every image a changed Markdown file names.

notes.body: A click closes a Radix tooltip. Here the click opens it, so a tap on a phone shows the reason too.
`<details>` is always open: a closed one could hide the change.

fileNotes.src/ui/PierreDiff.tsx: New `PierreSnippet` and `PierreSnippetDiff`: Pierre without line numbers, on a clear canvas. `SplitResizeHandle` is exported.
fileNotes.src/ui/components/MarkdownDiff.module.cs: The look of rendered tags, and the card under a code block.

groups.title: Rendered or Source
groups.summary: `HunkView` and the full file viewer (`Inspector`) show rendered Markdown in place of the Pierre source view, and one shared choice in `markdown-view.ts` switches every file.

notes.body: `null` rows mean a side could not be read; the file then shows its source diff.
A renamed file has another path at base. Image paths in the file are read from the path of the side shown.

fileNotes.src/ui/lib/markdown-view.ts: New: the choice, kept in `localStorage`; `rendered` when nothing is stored.
fileNotes.src/ui/App.tsx: The `m` key calls `toggleMarkdownView`, in the diff and in the full file viewer.

groups.title: An export keeps the highlighters of code fences
groups.summary: An export deletes the highlighter chunks the changed paths do not need. `markdownFences` now also reads the fence names of changed Markdown files, and the manifest maps a second name of a language to its chunk.

attention.note: The change in `vite-shiki-langs.ts` fixes a bug older than this PR: `zsh`, `yml`, `dockerfile`, and `makefile` had no entry in the manifest, so an export dropped the chunk they load and a `.sh` file had no colors. It now reads `bundledLanguagesInfo` from `shiki`. Check an export of a change with a `.sh` or `.yml` file.

notes.body: A line that only looks like a fence can match. The export then keeps one highlighter more than it needs.

fileNotes.src/api/markdown.ts: New: `isMarkdownPath` moved here from the UI, with the fence helpers the UI and the export share.
fileNotes.src/api/live.ts: `markdownFences` reads both sides of each changed Markdown file.

commits.subject: Markdown diff: an image path with a bare % keeps its other escapes
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: Markdown diff: review fixes
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body: - A hunk that only changes a code block no longer says only blank lines changed. - A worker that does not start, or does not take a job, gives the source diff. - An image that failed does not hide the next image in its place. - The full file viewer reads image paths from the path of the side shown. - A shows its ; a bare % in an image path does not drop the image. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2

commits.subject: Markdown diff: HTML, images, code blocks as line diffs, the full file viewer, and no limits on word marks
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
- The full file viewer has the Rendered / Source control, and m switches it there too.
- The word diff runs in a worker with fast-myers-diff, so it has no time limit. The 60% rule is
  gone: two changes join when the text kept between them is no longer than either, and a block
  with no word kept has no marks.
- HTML in Markdown is parsed into the same tree and cut down to what GitHub allows.
- Images load: a web address as it is, a path from the images of the change. A link or an image
  that does not open says why.
- A code block has the colors of its language. One with changed lines reads as a line diff.
- An export keeps the highlighters that code fences name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Export keeps the highlighter of a language with a second name
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A language such as zsh, yml or dockerfile is a second name for another
language and has no chunk of its own, so the manifest had no entry for it
and an export dropped the chunk it loads. A .sh file, and a sh code fence,
then had no colors in an exported review.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Markdown diff: an image whose path changed shows its source; a moved block keeps its look in a markup-only row
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: Markdown diff: show the source of a block when only its markup changed; keep table column alignment
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: Markdown files read as rendered prose in the diff
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A Markdown file's hunks render as Markdown: git's lines decide which blocks are removed and added, and the words that differ are marked inside them. Notes, comments, focus ranges, moved blocks, and the split layout work as they do in the source diff. A Rendered/Source control on each Markdown file, and the m key, switch every Markdown file; the choice is remembered.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

before.note: `wordMarks` marks no words in a block when more than 60% of its words changed (`REWRITE_SHARE`), and stops after 150 ms (`WORD_DIFF_MS`). Such a block shows only its red or green tint. Two unrelated texts of 9,000 words each took 11 s to compare without the limit. Decide if these two numbers fit your skill diffs.

after.note: `joinEdits` replaces the 60% rule and the 150 ms limit. summary.after: `MarkdownDiff` draws the rows in one column or two. A code block goes through Pierre (`PierreSnippet`, `PierreSnippetDiff`), an image loads from the web or from git, and a link that does not open says why.

before.note: The rendered view does not run HTML, fetch images, or follow relative links. `rawHtml` shows a tag such as `<kbd>` as its source, `img` shows the alt text, and a relative link is a styled `span`. Only `http`, `https`, and `mailto` links open. Decide if a reviewer needs to see images of the repository here.
